lines.zh: 你大概每天都在和它聊天：问问题、写代码、改文章。
lines.en: You probably chat with it every day: asking questions, writing code, editing essays.

lines.zh: 但你想过吗，它的内部到底在发生什么？
lines.en: But have you ever wondered what is actually happening inside it?

lines.zh: 这是「大语言模型」课程的第零章：导读。
lines.en: This is Chapter 0 of the Large Language Model course: the orientation.

lines.zh: 这一集不讲公式，只做一件事：给你一张地图。
lines.en: No formulas today. Just one job: give you a map.

lines.zh: 一张能装进脑子、也能随时翻回来的地图。
lines.en: A map that fits in your head, and that you can come back to.

lines.zh: 七十年的人工智能研究，能不能压缩成一句话？
lines.en: Can seventy years of AI research be squeezed into one sentence?

lines.zh: 可以。大语言模型，是用海量文本训练出来的程序。
lines.en: Yes. A large language model is a program trained on enormous amounts of text.

lines.zh: 它只擅长一件事：根据上文，猜下一个词。
lines.en: It is good at one thing: guessing the next word from the preceding text.

lines.zh: 你手机的输入法，其实每天都在做类似的事。
lines.en: The keyboard on your phone does something similar every day.

lines.zh: 比如这一句：今天下雨了，出门记得带……
lines.en: Take this sentence: It is raining, remember to bring your...

lines.zh: 下一个词，最可能是「伞」。
lines.en: The most likely next word is umbrella.

lines.zh: 但模型不是查表，它给每个候选词打分。
lines.en: But the model does not look up a table; it scores every candidate.

lines.zh: 挑一个接上，再把新词放回上文，继续猜。
lines.en: It picks one, appends it, puts it back into the context, and guesses again.

lines.zh: 目标很朴素，可当模型大到一定程度，奇怪的事发生了。
lines.en: The goal is plain. But once the model gets big enough, something strange happens.

lines.zh: 翻译、推理、写代码，没有人专门教过它。
lines.en: Translation, reasoning, coding: nobody taught it these directly.

lines.zh: 这些能力，是在预测下一个词的过程中长出来的。
lines.en: They grew out of the single task of predicting the next word.

lines.zh: 我们管它们叫：副产品。
lines.en: We call them by-products.

lines.zh: 不过，这句话里的每个词，都值得怀疑。
lines.en: But every word in that sentence deserves suspicion.

lines.zh: 第一，为什么猜下一个词，能逼出推理？
lines.en: First: why would guessing the next word produce reasoning?

lines.zh: 第二，「大到一定程度」到底是多大？
lines.en: Second: how big is big enough?

lines.zh: 为什么是突然变好，而不是慢慢变好？
lines.en: Why does it improve suddenly, instead of gradually?

lines.zh: 第三，猜得准，就等于理解吗？
lines.en: Third: does guessing well mean understanding?

lines.zh: 第四，如果它只是在猜，为什么会一本正经地胡说？
lines.en: Fourth: if it is only guessing, why does it state nonsense so confidently?

lines.zh: 整门课，就是把这四个问题，一层一层拆开。
lines.en: This whole course takes those four questions apart, layer by layer.

lines.zh: 拆完以后，你能读懂论文摘要，也能判断新闻有没有夸大。
lines.en: Afterwards, you can read a paper abstract and judge whether a headline exaggerates.

lines.zh: 先看地图。左边是目标，右边有五个模块。
lines.en: Start with the map. The goal is on the left; five modules are on the right.

lines.zh: 目标是预测下一个词；五个模块，是支撑它的柱子。
lines.en: The goal is predicting the next word; five modules are the pillars beneath it.

lines.zh: 表示：词怎么变成向量。
lines.en: Representation: how words become vectors.

lines.zh: 架构：Transformer 怎么组织计算。
lines.en: Architecture: how a Transformer organises computation.

lines.zh: 数据：互联网文本，怎么变成训练材料。
lines.en: Data: how internet text becomes training material.

lines.zh: 规模：为什么越大越好，还能讲出规律。
lines.en: Scale: why bigger is better, and why the law is predictable.

lines.zh: 对齐：怎么让它听人类的话。
lines.en: Alignment: how to make it follow human intent.

lines.zh: 如果只记五个词：预测、表示、架构、规模、对齐。
lines.en: If you remember only five words: prediction, representation, architecture, scale, alignment.

lines.zh: 这张地图，画了七十多年，大致分成五个时代。
lines.en: This map took over seventy years to draw, and falls into five eras.

lines.zh: 1948 到 2002：统计时代，靠数数估计下一个词的概率。
lines.en: 1948 to 2002: the statistical era, estimating next-word probabilities by counting.

lines.zh: 2003 到 2016：神经时代，神经网络代替数数，词也变成向量。
lines.en: 2003 to 2016: the neural era, replacing counts with networks and words with vectors.

lines.zh: 2017 到 2019：Transformer 时代，更并行，也更会看全局。
lines.en: 2017 to 2019: the Transformer era, more parallel, and aware of the whole context.

lines.zh: 2020 到 2022：规模时代，越大越好，背后有数学规律。
lines.en: 2020 to 2022: the scale era, where the rule that bigger is better follows a law.

lines.zh: 2022 年到现在：对齐与推理时代，从会说话，到听话，再到会想。
lines.en: 2022 to now: alignment and reasoning, from talking, to following, to thinking.

lines.zh: 注意，这些年代只是大致边界；五个时代，是同一条主线的五次换挡。
lines.en: Note: these dates are rough boundaries; five eras, five gear changes on one road.

lines.zh: 把五个时代放在一起看，有一个反复出现的模式。
lines.en: Put the five eras side by side and a pattern keeps returning.

lines.zh: 每一次跃迁，都是把一个手工设计的部件，换成从数据里学出来的部件。
lines.en: Every leap swaps a hand-designed part for a part learned from data.

lines.zh: 统计模型的回退规则是人写的，神经网络把它学了出来。
lines.en: Back-off rules were written by hand; neural networks learned them.

lines.zh: 循环网络逐词传递，是架构强加的限制，注意力把它放开了。
lines.en: Recurrent nets passed words one at a time; attention removed that limit.

lines.zh: 有用、无害、诚实，本来是人写的规则，RLHF 改成从比较里学。
lines.en: Helpful, harmless, honest were hand-written rules; RLHF learned them from comparisons.

lines.zh: 然后，再靠规模，把这个新部件推向质变。
lines.en: Then scale pushes the new part over a threshold.

lines.zh: 生物学里管这叫「预适应」：羽毛最初为了保暖，后来用来飞行。
lines.en: Biology calls this exaptation: feathers first for warmth, later for flight.

lines.zh: 说完内容，再说这门课怎么写。
lines.en: Now, how is this course written?

lines.zh: 很多教程，第一章讲 softmax，第四章再讲一遍，第九章又讲一遍。
lines.en: Many tutorials explain softmax in chapter one, again in four, again in nine.

lines.zh: 这门课换了个做法：每个概念只定义一次。
lines.en: This course does it differently: each concept is defined once.

lines.zh: 第一次出现时，给定义、给直觉、给一个例子，然后登记进概念账本。
lines.en: When a concept first appears, it gets a definition, an intuition, an example, and a ledger entry.

lines.zh: 之后再见，只写「见某节」，不再解释。
lines.en: Later chapters simply point back to that section.

lines.zh: 每章开头，还会写清「新增」了什么，「前置」需要什么。
lines.en: Every chapter opens with what is new and what is assumed.

lines.zh: 同一个例子，也绝不用第二次。
lines.en: And no example is ever used twice.

lines.zh: 因为工作记忆很有限，重复会挤掉真正的新东西。
lines.en: Working memory is limited; repetition crowds out what is truly new.

lines.zh: 最后，换一个角度看这些零件。
lines.en: Finally, look at these parts from another angle.

lines.zh: 熵来自热力学，被信息论借走，最后成了训练模型的损失函数。
lines.en: Entropy came from thermodynamics, was borrowed by information theory, and became the loss.

lines.zh: 梯度下降，和细菌朝着养分游动，是同一个算法。
lines.en: Gradient descent is the same algorithm as bacteria swimming toward nutrients.

lines.zh: 混合专家模型，就是亚当·斯密别针工厂里的分工。
lines.en: Mixture of experts is the division of labour in Adam Smith's pin factory.

lines.zh: 生物学里的预适应，也是同一个模式：旧结构，新用途。
lines.en: Biology's exaptation is the same pattern: an old structure, a new use.

lines.zh: 类比是迁移知识的好工具，但也可能是陷阱；所以每个类比，我们都会标出它在哪里失效。
lines.en: Analogy is a powerful tool for transfer, and also a trap; so we mark where it breaks down.

lines.zh: 地图讲完了，但地图不等于地形。
lines.en: The map is done. But a map is not the terrain.

lines.zh: 开始之前，请带上三样东西。
lines.en: Before we start, bring three things.

lines.zh: 一点耐心：第二章的反向传播、第五章的注意力，是两个陡坡。
lines.en: Patience: backpropagation in chapter two and attention in chapter five are the steep climbs.

lines.zh: 一支笔：自测先写答案，再看解析；看懂不等于会做。
lines.en: A pen: write your self-test answers before reading mine; understanding is not doing.

lines.zh: 还有怀疑精神：找不到出处的说法，一律当作待验证。
lines.en: And skepticism: any claim without a source counts as unverified.

lines.zh: 下一章，我们把「猜下一个词」，写成一个可以计算的概率问题。
lines.en: Next chapter, we turn guessing the next word into a computable probability problem.

lines.zh: 顺便解释，为什么衡量猜得好不好，要用到「熵」。
lines.en: Along the way, we'll see why judging how well it guesses calls for entropy.

lines.zh: 第一章，语言的概率论。我们下期见。
lines.en: Chapter one: the probability theory of language. See you next time.
